raw_findings.body: JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery filters group membership by these values, but they are authorization Resource UUIDs, not group IDs (the group id is stored as the resource *name* by AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup). The membership subquery matches nothing, so the search returns zero users even though the admin has member-view permission.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent wrong result: user search/count returns an empty or incorrect user list for group-scoped admins.
raw_findings.impact: JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery filters group membership by these values, but they are authorization Resource UUIDs, not group IDs (the group id is stored as the resource *name* by AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup). The membership subquery matches nothing, so the search returns zero users even though the admin has member-view permission.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new V2 implementation conflates the authorization Resource primary key with the group identifier that V2 stores in the resource name.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `groupResource.getName()` (which holds the group id for V2 resources) instead of `groupResource.getId()` to the `granted` set.
raw_findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz Resource IDs instead of group IDs
raw_findings.trigger: An admin without view-users/manage-users but with a Groups permission granting VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS calls GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users (UsersResource.searchForUser), which puts the returned set into session attribute UserModel.GROUPS.

raw_findings.body: hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves the resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId); passing the Resource UUID never matches a resource name, so the lookup falls back to the all-groups resource and returns false for every group, leaving the granted set empty and the per-group member-view permissions ignored in the DB query.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Permission evaluation silently short-circuits to false, producing incorrect filtering of the user query.
raw_findings.impact: hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves the resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId); passing the Resource UUID never matches a resource name, so the lookup falls back to the all-groups resource and returns false for every group, leaving the granted set empty and the per-group member-view permissions ignored in the DB query.
raw_findings.root_cause: Mismatch between the identifier hasPermission expects (resource name == group id) and the identifier supplied by the findByType callback (resource id).
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `groupResource.getName()` (the group id) to hasPermission, or refactor hasPermission to accept a Resource directly for this iteration.
raw_findings.title: hasPermission called with Resource ID where a group ID (resource name) is expected
raw_findings.trigger: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is invoked (user search/count for an admin lacking view-users) while group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS permissions exist for individual groups.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test design critique claiming MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scope enforcement isn't properly isolated. The test does grant both permissions before the positive assertion, but this is a test coverage opinion rather than a concrete defect. The test still verifies the feature works when permissions are granted.

validated_findings.body: The test only checks that no exception is thrown; a server change that authorizes the call but does not persist the membership would still pass, leaving the feature silently untested.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Weak coverage: positive path is not verified beyond absence of ForbiddenException.
validated_findings.impact: The test only checks that no exception is thrown; a server change that authorizes the call but does not persist the membership would still pass, leaving the feature silently untested.
validated_findings.root_cause: Test terminates on an action instead of an observable assertion.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Assert the resulting state, e.g. `assertThat(realm.admin().groups().group(topGroup.getId()).members(), hasItem(matching bob))` or check `realm.admin().users().get(bobId).groups()` contains topGroup.
validated_findings.title: No assertion that the membership change actually took effect
validated_findings.trigger: testManageGroupMembership ends with the joinGroup call and no verification step.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that joinGroup success isn't verified is a test quality suggestion, not a defect. The test verifies authorization works by checking the call doesn't throw ForbiddenException. Verifying persistence is a different concern and the test's purpose is authorization checking.

validated_findings.body: The over-permissive behaviour of GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), which returns true when only AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW is granted, is not detected: a VIEW-only admin could create/update groups and the new test suite would still be green.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Privilege-escalation behaviour in the evaluated scopes remains uncovered by the added tests.
validated_findings.impact: The over-permissive behaviour of GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), which returns true when only AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW is granted, is not detected: a VIEW-only admin could create/update groups and the new test suite would still be green.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new view-oriented test omits negative management assertions for the VIEW-only state.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a negative assertion in testViewGroups that, with only VIEW granted, `groups().add(...)` / `groups().group(id).update(...)` is rejected with FORBIDDEN.
validated_findings.title: testViewGroups never asserts that a VIEW-only grant denies group management
validated_findings.trigger: After granting only the VIEW scope for all groups, the test performs solely read operations (groups() listing) and finishes.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage suggestion about adding negative management assertions for VIEW-only grants. While related to the canManage() bug in candidate 2, this finding is about missing test coverage rather than a concrete defect in the patch code itself.
